project.title: AstraBuild: A Longitudinal Evaluation of GPT-6 Astra as a 3D Engineering Agent

authority_sources.path_or_reference: release/behavior_analysis.json (from scripts/analyze_process_behavior.py over read-only historical batch folders)

contract.gap: Existing 3D reconstruction and generation results do not by themselves show whether a general-purpose reasoning model can form, test, and revise engineering hypotheses when registered physical evidence contradicts its current representation in a persistent engineering environment.
contract.task: Evaluate GPT-6 Astra as a model-in-harness across heterogeneous component-level substation reconstruction tasks, focusing on how it selects measurement problems and representations, revises higher-level engineering assumptions after contradiction, and maintains accepted outputs in persistent state.
outcomes: recurring failure boundaries in detail and coordinate semantics

questions.text: When a general-purpose reasoning model is constrained by registered geometric evidence, programmatic tools, and deterministic validation in a persistent 3D environment, how does it form, test, and revise engineering hypotheses, and where do those decisions fail?

contract.contribution: A longitudinal evaluation of one general-purpose reasoning model in a persistent 3D engineering harness, using heterogeneous reconstruction tasks as behavioral probes, preserved cases to analyze hypothesis revision and failure modes, and station-scale composition as a long-horizon stress test.
nonclaims: not an estimate of population-wide failure frequencies from the selected behavioral cases
not proof that internal model chain-of-thought is recoverable from historical artifacts

semantic_locks.canonical: study how Astra forms, tests, and revises engineering hypotheses under registered evidence, external tools, deterministic validation, and persistent state; characterize where those decisions fail
longitudinal single-site case study; later batches inherit earlier engineering state
D38.2 is the core geometry baseline; D40 is presentation-only and geometry-invariant; D41 is the additive inspection-semantic endpoint
reference-surface residuals are against the same photogrammetric mesh used during reconstruction and are not independent survey accuracy
human feedback materially affects B08, B36, D38 and semantic audit decisions; the workflow is human-steerable rather than fully autonomous
Codex + GPT-6 Astra Extra High is owner-confirmed experimental metadata; old batch manifests do not independently freeze the model configuration

terminology.preferred: editable component-level station model / digital twin

style_profile.language_variant: English research prose with Chinese parallel translation on website

facts.value: 79 accessory meshes; 17 selected inspection-relevant classes on T1 and T2

alignment.method: One GPT-6 Astra/Codex model-in-harness is observed across 38 dependent core batches and 12 reconstruction task families. Evidence is externalized through registered geometry, images, records, diagnostics, original review pages, deterministic validation, and persistent batch state.
alignment.evidence: Task-native metrics; B01/B15/B23/B25-B26/B36/D38 adaptation/failure episodes; B32 fine-detail interpretation trace; behavior_analysis.json; 32 historical reviews; 40 process dossiers; D38.2/D40 composition state.
alignment.result: Astra can formulate and invoke explicit measurement procedures and can revise protocol, abstraction, representation, and task-selection decisions when contradictions are externalized. Fine-detail and coordinate-semantic interpretations remain error-prone; human steering and deterministic validation materially affect acceptance.
alignment.interpretation: The supported role is a human-steerable engineering reasoner inside a deterministic reconstruction system rather than an autonomous reconstruction authority.
alignment.limitation: Single site; correlated photogrammetric reference rather than independent survey truth; dependent batches; heterogeneous validators; selected behavioral episodes are descriptive; no matched second-model or expert baseline; legacy model configuration is owner-confirmed.
alignment.contribution: Tasks are used as behavioral probes, preserved cases explain how modeling hypotheses change, and station composition tests persistent state over a long horizon.

decisions.decision: Website should read as an interactive technical report, not a product landing page or benchmark dashboard.
Original batch review.html pages are primary task-level qualitative evidence.
Kimi/specialist 3D baselines are out of scope for the current advisor-discussion draft.
Website prose follows the project-scoped academic-writing-skills review contract; the final website prose candidate passed stock-prose and text-consistency audits on 2026-09-16.

v0.8 reframes paper and website from outcome presentation to behavioral analysis of the agent under test, modeled on the robodojo gpt-6-astra-eval report style: model/harness decoupling, E1-E3 occupancy taxonomy, findings-first structure, negative results front-loaded. Paper lands as new file paper_v08_analysis.md (v0.7 retained as REFERENCE); website rewritten in place; tex sync deferred until venue decision.

issues.description: No independent survey/LiDAR truth; geometric residuals use correlated photogrammetric reference. This is retained as an explicit validity limitation and claim boundary.
Single-site longitudinal case does not establish cross-site generalization. This is retained as an explicit scope limitation.
Legacy batch records do not independently freeze model/reasoning-effort metadata; the current manuscript labels the configuration as owner-confirmed metadata.
